prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one 4:3 landscape painting for The Burnt Book Sanskrit learning story. Request 1536 x 1152 native output or the closest supported native 4:3 resolution. Refined Indian watercolor with restrained gouache on warm ivory paper; organic detail, quiet ochre, sage, dusty terracotta, muted indigo. Warm, gentle, evocative storytelling, consistent character design.
Canonical scene brief: The school library at night, moonlight through a window: a small blue-black spirit with ink-stained wisps writing in the air with a reed pen, faint glowing lines of verse trailing behind it; you, Dādī and Śuka peering round a shelf; the tree of names glowing softly in a corner.
Character appearances:
you: Always seen from behind or at a distance, face never detailed, so every learner can be the hero: a young person in a simple ochre kurta with a cloth shoulder bag.
dadi: A warm, sharp-eyed grandmother in her seventies, silver hair in a low bun, round spectacles, a cream cotton sari with a thin maroon border and a grey shawl; carries a cloth-bound notebook.
shuka: A bright green rose-ringed parrot with a red beak and a faint pink and black neck ring, a little scruffy, very expressive eyes; usually on your shoulder or Dādī's.
acarya: A very old, serene scholar with a white beard and a saffron shawl, a palm-leaf manuscript always under his arm, kind half-closed eyes.
kavika: A small blue-black spirit with ink-stained wisps, a reed pen behind one ear.
Phone-first composition: clear compact narrative grouping, essential faces, hands and objects comfortably inside all edges. Show the complete scene without border. No collage or multi-panel layout.
Owner-approved writing: render the following EXACT text, and no other writing, on the physical surface described in the scene. Use generous size, clear orthographic shapes and accurate Devanagari. The same text remains live app content. Do not substitute, omit, add or invent letters. No watermark, UI or extra labels.
कविः कवी कवयः। All human and humanoid figures wear complete opaque traditional clothing or robes.

image.brief: The school library at night, moonlight through a window: a small blue-black spirit with ink-stained wisps writing in the air with a reed pen, faint glowing lines of verse trailing behind it; you, Dādī and Śuka peering round a shelf; the tree of names glowing softly in a corner.

alt.en: An ink-stained spirit writing glowing verse in the air in a moonlit library
alt.hi: चाँदनी में पुस्तकालय में हवा पर चमकते श्लोक लिखता स्याही से सना भूत

narration.en: Late that night, while the school sleeps, scratching comes from the library. A small blue-black spirit with ink on every wisp is writing on the air with a reed pen, muttering verses. Every line ends the same way, in -इ. “कविः,” he says, tapping his own chest. “कवयः,” he adds, looking round hopefully at a shelf of silent bundles.
narration.hi: उस रात देर से, जब पाठशाला सोती है, पुस्तकालय से खरोंच की आवाज़ आती है। हर लट पर स्याही लगा एक नन्हा नीला-काला भूत सरकंडे की कलम से हवा पर लिख रहा है, श्लोक बुदबुदाते हुए। हर पंक्ति एक ही ढंग से समाप्त होती है, -इ पर। “कविः,” वह अपनी छाती थपथपाकर कहता है। “कवयः,” वह जोड़ता है, चुप गट्ठरों की अलमारी की ओर आशा से देखता हुआ।

gloss.hi: एक कवि, दो कवि, अनेक कवि।

body.en: Many words end in a short -{{इ}}: {{कवि}} (poet), {{अग्नि}} (fire), {{मुनि}} (sage) are masculine; {{मति}} (thought), {{भूमि}} (earth), {{रात्रि}} (night) are feminine. Their patterns are close to {{देव}} and {{लता}}, with the {{इ}} sometimes turning to {{ए}} or {{य्}}.
body.hi: अनेक शब्द ह्रस्व -{{इ}} पर समाप्त होते हैं: {{कवि}}, {{अग्नि}}, {{मुनि}} पुंलिंग हैं; {{मति}}, {{भूमि}}, {{रात्रि}} स्त्रीलिंग हैं। उनका ढाँचा {{देव}} और {{लता}} के क़रीब है, जिसमें {{इ}} कभी {{ए}} या {{य्}} बन जाता है।

caption.en: A poet, in every case and number
caption.hi: कवि, हर विभक्ति और वचन में

note.en: The {{इ}} becomes {{ए}} or {{अय्}} before many endings: {{कवये}}, {{कवयः}}, {{हे कवे}}.
note.hi: कई प्रत्ययों से पहले {{इ}} {{ए}} या {{अय्}} बन जाता है: {{कवये}}, {{कवयः}}, {{हे कवे}}।

caption.en: A thought, in every case and number
caption.hi: मति, हर विभक्ति और वचन में

note.en: The feminine has optional forms in the singular: {{मतये}} or {{मत्यै}}, {{मतेः}} or {{मत्याः}}, {{मतौ}} or {{मत्याम्}}. The first of each is shown.
note.hi: स्त्रीलिंग में एकवचन के वैकल्पिक रूप हैं: {{मतये}} या {{मत्यै}}, {{मतेः}} या {{मत्याः}}, {{मतौ}} या {{मत्याम्}}। हर एक का पहला रूप दिखाया है।

prompt.en: Fill in the missing forms of the table.

explain.en: Every form is in the table you just read.
explain.hi: हर रूप उसी तालिका में है जो अभी पढ़ी।

prompt.en: Fill in the missing forms of a feminine in -इ.
prompt.hi: -इ वाले एक स्त्रीलिंग के छूटे रूप भरिए।

prompt.en: Join each form to its case and number.
prompt.hi: हर रूप को उसकी विभक्ति और वचन से जोड़िए।

prompt.en: Tap every form of {{कवि}} that has {{अय्}}: {{कवयः}} or {{कवये}}.
prompt.hi: {{कवि}} के हर रूप को छुइए जिसमें {{अय्}} है: {{कवयः}} या {{कवये}}।

success.en: “कवयः,” you say, and the shelf of silent bundles trembles. A dozen faint voices, long dead poets, answer in chorus: “कवयः!” The little spirit beams, ink dripping from his chin.
success.hi: “कवयः,” आप कहते हैं, और चुप गट्ठरों की अलमारी काँपती है। एक दर्जन धीमी आवाज़ें, कब के मरे कवि, सामूहिक रूप से उत्तर देती हैं: “कवयः!” नन्हा भूत खिल उठता है, ठुड्डी से स्याही टपकती हुई।

failure.en: The shelf stays silent. Plural: the {{इ}} becomes {{अय्}} and takes {{अः}}.
failure.hi: अलमारी चुप रहती है। बहुवचन: {{इ}} {{अय्}} बनता है और {{अः}} लेता है।

body.en: Why {{कवयः}} and not {{कविः}} again? Sūtra 7.3.109, {{जसि च}}, strengthens a final {{इ}}/{{उ}} to {{ए}}/{{ओ}} before the plural ending {{जस्}}; and {{ए}} becomes {{अय्}} before a vowel. In the singular call, 6.1.69, {{एङ्ह्रस्वात् सम्बुद्धेः}}, drops the ending after {{ए}}.
body.hi: {{कवयः}} क्यों, फिर {{कविः}} क्यों नहीं? सूत्र 7.3.109, {{जसि च}}, बहुवचन प्रत्यय {{जस्}} से पहले अन्तिम {{इ}}/{{उ}} को {{ए}}/{{ओ}} बना देता है; और {{ए}} स्वर से पहले {{अय्}} हो जाता है। सम्बोधन एकवचन में 6.1.69, {{एङ्ह्रस्वात् सम्बुद्धेः}}, {{ए}} के बाद प्रत्यय हटा देता है।
